correctness.rationale: The proof independently establishes that F2-independent solutions of x^[2]=Ax are F_q-independent by applying Frobenius to a minimal F_q-dependence, bounding solution dimension by n. Counting ordered solution frames gives E F_k(D)=1 for every k=0..n over any F_{2^m}, equal to the GL_n(F2) fixedspace moments. An upper-triangular nonzero-diagonal moment matrix proves equality of distributions; subspace Möbius inversion yields exact nonnegative integral counts. For n=3 P0=48/168=2/7, distinct from S7 derangements 1854/5040=103/280. Standalone checker verifies every GL matrix in six small configurations, and exact symbolic counts through dimension 12. No finite sample is treated as proof.

originality.rationale: The full distribution and binary-field-size invariance are not implied by the 2026 average-one result. Exact n=3 characteristic-two probability 2/7 contradicts 103/280 symmetric-group derangements predicted under an unrestricted-q interpretation of its conjectural consequence; the characteristic-zero Galois-group claim is not refuted. Semilinear normal forms and fixed-space counts are acknowledged as prior components. Both related primary full papers were read. Targeted mathematical record searches found no directly equivalent distribution, while historical fixed-subspace literature leaves a genuine risk.

value.rationale: Random idempotent counts are explicitly motivated by a current survey, which had obtained only their average. The result supplies a uniform all-rank exact probability law across every finite binary extension, distinguishes individual counts rather than a first moment, and proves the characteristic-two exception to an unrestricted large-q fixed-point prediction in dimension three. The contrast identifies a necessary characteristic qualification for subsequent Galois/statistical formulations. It is not a routine field-size substitution or a small isolated table.
